whyItMatters: Severely impacted stool can block the bowel and press on the colon wall. Ulceration and perforation of the stretched colon are serious risks.

findings: AP or PA projection abdominal/chest radiograph showing the lower thorax and entire abdomen
A massive, lobulated, heterogeneous soft-tissue mass occupying virtually the entire abdomen and lower hemithorax, predominantly left-sided but crossing midline
The mass has a coarse, mixed-density internal architecture with innumerable small lucencies throughout, suggesting cystic or necrotic components interspersed with soft-tissue/calcific elements
The mass displaces bowel gas peripherally; normal bowel gas pattern is markedly distorted
The right hemidiaphragm appears elevated; left hemidiaphragm is obscured by the mass
Right lower lung base shows atelectasis or compressive change
A large rounded gas-containing structure is visible in the left upper quadrant superiorly, possibly representing a gas-filled stomach displaced superiorly
The spine is visible centrally and appears midline without obvious destructive lesion on this view
No obvious rib destruction is identified on this projection
The right abdomen shows displacement of colonic/bowel gas laterally and inferiorly
differential: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma): massive abdominal mass with heterogeneous cystic-solid internal architecture in the expected renal fossa region, most common large abdominal mass with this appearance
Neuroblastoma: large retroperitoneal mass with heterogeneous/calcific components crossing midline, typical age-group presentation
Hepatoblastoma or other primary hepatic tumor with massive hepatomegaly and heterogeneous density, though the distribution appears more left-sided and retroperitoneal than typical hepatic origin
anatomyConcerns: The sheer size of the mass makes it difficult to determine organ of origin on this single projection; cross-sectional imaging would be required
Bowel gas is severely displaced, limiting assessment of bowel distribution
Left hemidiaphragm position cannot be confirmed due to mass overlap
No lateral projection is available to assess anterior-posterior extent or depth of the lesion

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The image shows a massive heterogeneous mottled mass with innumerable small gas lucencies distributed throughout the entire abdomen, consistent with impacted stool (faecaloma) within a massively dilated colon. The speckled bubble pattern is characteristic of trapped gas within impacted faecal material, not the cystic-necrotic architecture of a solid tumour. The clinical context of chronic gut-slowing medication, weeks of abdominal swelling, vomiting, and months without bowel movement strongly supports faecaloma. The independent differential (Wilms, neuroblastoma, hepatoblastoma) applies to a paediatric population and is inconsistent with the adult clinical vignette. The mottled gas pattern throughout the mass, following a colonic distribution, distinguishes faecaloma from a solid retroperitoneal or renal mass.
